## Summary

I implemented SPEC.md §5 (Transcribe / Speech) using the iOS Speech framework directly:

- **`app/services/speech.ts`** (new) — wraps `SFSpeechRecognizer`/`SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` for authorization status/request and file-based transcription with partial results, mirroring the existing `services/health.ts` pattern.
- **`app/components/Transcribe.vue`** — wired the placeholder screen to the service: exact status-line labels per §5.2, button enable/disable rules per §5.3, live-updating transcript area, and a `Completed in N.N s` line measured from tap to final result.
- **`vite.config.ts`** — added a static-copy plugin target so `spec-assets/sample.wav` (untouched) is bundled into the app at `assets/sample.wav`, loaded at runtime via `knownFolders.currentApp()`.
- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`.
- **`package.json`** — added `vite-plugin-static-copy` (already resolvable via the existing NativeScript/Vite toolchain, now declared explicitly).

`ns build ios` succeeds and `vue-tsc --noEmit` is clean. I drove the app on the Simulator with `idb`/`simctl`: navigation, the authorization dialog (showing our exact usage string), and the granted status all work correctly. Tapping "Transcribe Sample" exercises the real recognition path, but the Simulator's speech service fails with `kAFAssistantErrorDomain 1101` ("Failed to initialize recognizer") — a well-documented iOS Simulator limitation where the local speech-recognition daemon lacks installed language assets, unrelated to app code (confirmed via `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = false`, explicit `en-US` locale, and a full simulator reboot — none change the outcome). Importantly, the app handles this exactly per spec §5.3's failure path: the error surfaces as human-readable text in the status line, the button re-enables, and there's no crash.

Per this project's definition of done (build succeeds, app runs without crashing), the task is complete. The end-to-end success path (streaming partial transcript → final transcript matching the reference) will need verification on a real device or a Simulator with working speech services, since that's outside what this sandboxed environment can exercise.
